wars.outcome: Peace of Münster, 30 January 1648: Spain 'recognised the Dutch Republic as an independent country' and 'retained the Southern Netherlands'; the Dutch demands were 'generally met', including 'cession of the Meierij'.
wars.note: Infobox 'c. 1566/1568 - 30 January 1648'. Territorial changes on the Dutch side by year: Antwerp lost 1585; Breda 1590; Zutphen, Deventer, Delfzijl, Nijmegen 1591; Steenwijk, Coevorden 1592; Groningen 1594; Grol, Enschede, Ootmarsum, Oldenzaal 1597; Ostend lost 1604; Breda lost 1625 and retaken 1637; Oldenzaal 1626, Groenlo 1627, 's-Hertogenbosch 1629; Venlo, Roermond, Maastricht 1632; Sas van Gent 1644, Hulst 1645. Twelve Years' Truce 9 April 1609 to 1621. The war ran c. 1566/1568 to 30 January 1648; from is clipped to the Republic's start (1582) by reviewer eu-09-j (brief rule: wars inside the life).

wars.name: Franco-Dutch War

zones.text: Utrecht (French from June 1672), Overijssel (Münster from June 1672), Groningen (besieged 21 July-27 August 1672) and Maastricht (French from 30 June 1673)

wars.outcome: The Treaty of Nijmegen (10 August 1678): the Dutch 'ended the war without losing an inch of their own territory' and 'regained all the territory lost at the beginning'; peace with England (Treaty of Westminster, February 1674), Münster (April 1674) and Cologne (May 1674) came earlier.
wars.note: In May 1672 'France nearly overran the Netherlands' (Rampjaar). Utrecht was occupied June 1672 to late 1673, Naarden 19 June 1672 to September 1673, Overijssel June 1672 to April 1674; Maastricht fell on 30 June 1673 and, with Grave, was the last French holding in 1674.

wars.note: All the territory changed hands overseas; the Republic's own land was untouched.

wars.note: The page dates the invasion to June 1787 and sends the troops to restore the stadtholder.

wars.outcome: 'Prince Frederick capitulated on 4 November' 1794; the garrison marched out on 7 November.
wars.note: The siege opened on 22 September 1794; the Dutch soldiers appear in the defending garrison.

wars.name: Batavian Revolution
wars.outcome: 'In the severe winter of 1794/'95 a French army with some Patriot Dutch units invaded over the frozen frontier rivers'; William V fled on 18 January and the Batavian Republic was proclaimed on 19 January 1795; the Treaty of The Hague (16 May 1795) imposed territorial concessions.
wars.note: The Batavian Revolution page gives only the year 1795 for the proclamation; the dates are from the Batavian Republic page. The territories the French took are not listed on either.

certainty.note: A war-time front with the Spanish Netherlands: Breda, Groningen, Ostend, Zeelandic Flanders and the Meuse towns changed hands town by town and the page draws no frontier line. The Twelve Years' Truce (1609-1621) froze the front but fixed no boundary.

Treaty borders after the Peace of Münster (30 January 1648), confirmed at Nijmegen (1678), Utrecht (1713) and Aix-la-Chapelle (1748). The exceptions are the condominium of Maastricht (shared with the Prince-Bishopric of Liège), the Barrier garrisons in the Austrian Netherlands 1715-1781 and Drenthe, a poor eighth area outside the States General: each stays approximate.
The French invasion of the winter of 1794/95 moved the front day by day to the proclamation of the Batavian Republic.

notes: Written by eu-09-j on 2026-10-25 from 14 pages (budget 14; the Flanders campaign page proved a disambiguation page and the Peace of Münster page was thin). ABOUT THE ROW: Cliopatria's Dutch Republic row (1582-1795, 42 shapes) is the Republic's own land plus its overseas holdings plus one stray cell. (1) The Orange cell: every shape contains one cell at Orange in Provence (44.2 N, 5.0 E); the Principality of Orange page shows a sovereign principality of William of Nassau inside the Empire, ceded to France in 1713, and the Dutch Republic page never mentions it; Cliopatria's own Principality of Orange row ends in 1571. (2) The overseas cells from 1600 (Pulicat, Moluccas, Batavia, Gold Coast, Gorée, Taiwan, Mauritius, Malacca, Ceylon, Bengal, Malabar, Java and the rest of Indonesia: 3 to 900 cells per shape). The Dutch Empire page says the VOC and WIC 'exercis[ed] quasi-governmental powers to negotiate treaties, wage war, administer territory', so every keyframe is clipped to 300 km of the Low Countries ({"intersect": [Cliopatria shape, circle 5.4 E 52.0 N 300 km]}), which keeps the Republic's core and drops both. This follows the note of the se-03-x batch in dutch-east-india-company ('the eu-09 review of that row should drop the overseas cells so this dossier and dutch-malacca are not drawn twice'). Overseas clusters with a colony dossier: Indonesia (dutch-east-india-company and the sultanate dossiers), Taiwan (dutch-formosa), Sri Lanka (dutch-ceylon), Malacca coast (dutch-malacca), Gold Coast (dutch-gold-coast). WITHOUT A DOSSIER, so they will vanish from the map until one is written: Dutch Coromandel (Pulicat, 2 cells from 1600 and 4 from 1612), Dutch Bengal (1 cell from 1659; the Dutch Empire page has 'Dutch Bengal 1627-1825'), Dutch Malabar (Cochin and Cannanore coast, about 13 cells from 1670; the page has 'Malabar 1665-1795' and 'Cranganore and Cochin in 1662'), Dutch Mauritius (5 cells 1640-1712; the page has 'Mauritius 1638-1710'), Gorée (2 to 13 cells, 1619-1652), Timor and the Aru and Kai islands (inside the Indonesia cluster; the VOC dossier says Timor is not on its pages). WHAT THE CORE IS: 130 to 156 cells (about 33,000-39,000 km2), no area given on the Dutch Republic page, so the infobox comparison could not be made; the Generality Lands page says the Generality lands were 'about one fifth of the Republic's total territory'. CORE SHAPE HISTORY: every Cliopatria core change before 1790 is covered by an event or marked unverified: 1582-1588 (Spanish reconquest: Antwerp 1585 sourced, the rest conf 1), 1588-1600 (recaptures, all sourced), 1600-1609 (Ostend 1604, Spinola 1605-06 sourced; 13 other cells unexplained, conf 1), 1612-1622 (unexplained, conf 1), 1626-1645 (sourced), 1648 (Generality Lands), 1673-1678 (occupations, Maastricht), 1794-95. Cell flicker after 1713 (1-3 cells at 1713, 1721, 1734, 1757, 1762) is noise, not a border move. KEY JUDGEMENTS TO CHECK: (a) the 1672 invasion is modelled as occupation (hatched), not as the 35-cell loss Cliopatria draws in 1673-76; (b) Cliopatria's 1794-95 shape also drops Zeeland, a quarter of Gelderland and two thirds of South Holland, which no page opened supports (the invasion crossed the frozen rivers in the winter of 1794/95; the Republic fell on 19 January 1795); the correction removes only Staats-Brabant, Staats-Vlaanderen, Maastricht, Venlo and Echt; (c) the start year is 1582 (Cliopatria) although the Act of Abjuration is 26 July 1581 (the Union of Utrecht dossier ends then) and the page dates the Republic to the instruction of 12 April 1588. RULERS: none written; the Republic had stadtholders (Maurice 1584-1625, Frederick 1625-1647, William II 1647-1650, William III 1672-1702, William IV 1747-1751, William V 1751-1795 on the infobox, with stadtholderless periods) and Grand Pensionaries, not rulers; the sovereign body was the States General. COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: habsburg-netherlands (the Spanish then Austrian Netherlands, which the eu-09 scope names but no group owns: 'Owned: (none)' in eu-09-x), prince-bishopric-of-munster (1672-74 occupier of Overijssel), and the overseas dossiers above. Pages that failed: none (the Flanders campaign URL is a disambiguation page and the Peace of Münster page lacks the terms).
